$description: Design tokens extracted from the claude.ai/design project 'lab-workshop' (TechDays: AI Fluency - Agentic Agents). W3C Design Tokens Community Group format (draft). Every token carries an $extensions.com.patterson.source naming the file it was extracted from. Where an extracted value conflicts with the 2025 Brand Guide, the Brand Guide value is in $value and the project's value is recorded in $extensions.com.patterson.conflict. Nothing is invented; gaps are recorded in _tbd and in DESIGN.md section 5.

com.patterson.meta.authoritativeSource: Patterson Companies Brand Guide, VERSION 3.2025 (2025-04-08), as encoded in patterson-corp/plugins/patterson-brand/skills/design-tokens/assets/tokens.json
com.patterson.meta.incubation: This extraction lives in patterson-labs as a recorded default, not a settled decision. Whether this design project or the existing patterson-brand design system supersedes the other is unresolved and escalated; see _SOURCES.md.
com.patterson.meta.siblingSnapshot: The Patterson Academy project binds the SAME design system UUID under the slug patterson-companies-design-system. This snapshot is the later of the two: it adds a production-verified layer and corrects two of the Academy snapshot's own choices. See the academy-design-tokens skill.

sourceKeys.LABDECK: lab-workshop handoff export, top-level ai-fluency-agentic-agents.css and the deck HTML it styles
sourceKeys.LABPROD: Values the snapshot labels VERIFIED / PRODUCTION, describing itself as read from the live pattersondental.com / pattersonvet.com theme stylesheet. Second-hand: the snapshot's claim, not an independent read.
sourceKeys.BG25: Patterson Companies Brand Guide, VERSION 3.2025 - authoritative
sourceKeys.DS20: DesignSystem_042120.pdf - UX design system and governance, April 2020
sourceKeys.DPL: Patterson Digital Pattern Library v5.7.2 toolkit.css - production stylesheet
sourceKeys.CORP: patterson-corp/plugins/patterson-brand/skills/design-tokens - the reference extraction these values are reconciled against

color.$description: The project's palette, reconciled against BG25. The eleven brand hexes are byte-identical to BG25 p.24. Everything this snapshot adds beyond the Academy one is an interaction state or a production alias.

brand.$description: Primary, secondary and tertiary brand palette. The snapshot's tokens/colors.css reproduces BG25 p.24 exactly, PMS annotations included. No reconciliation was needed.

navy.$description: Primary. Headings at every level, dark grounds, and this snapshot's primary button fill - see color.interaction.

sky.$description: Primary. Accent, focus ring, stat numeral. BG25 p.57 makes it the default button fill; this snapshot does not - the headline conflict of this import.

blue.$description: Secondary. Link colour and informational hue.

blueLight.$description: Secondary. This snapshot's secondary button fill.

tint.$description: CONFLICT, resolved for BG25. BG25 p.24 publishes a three-step 75/50/25 ramp over white; the values below are CORP's sampling of it and are what ships. The snapshot instead defines a five-step 80/60/40/20/10 ramp for navy and sky only - unchanged from the Academy snapshot. Both are consistent mixes over white at different stops, so no value is wrong; the step set is a brand decision and BG25 owns it.

$extensions.com.patterson.conflict: LABWS tokens/colors.css ships navy 80/60/40/20/10 = #335f85 / #6687a4 / #99afc2 / #ccd7e1 / #e5ebf0 and sky 80/60/40/20/10 = #33b9e7 / #66caed / #99dcf3 / #ccedf9 / #e5f6fc. Superseded by the BG25 ramp. Note the deck stylesheet consumes --pat-navy-40 and --pat-navy-60 directly - see color.deck.

neutral.$description: The snapshot's cool-grey ramp, plus the one warm neutral it adds. BG25 publishes only two greys (#58585B, #ECECEC); the rest is the project's own. [TBD: not specified in BG25.]

ink.$description: Near-black. Retained as a ramp step. Unlike the Academy snapshot, THIS snapshot does not wire it to headings - its own base.css corrects headings to navy, annotating that production sets every heading level navy.

warm.$description: A warm taupe - the one non-cool grey in the set. The snapshot marks it VERIFIED and uses it for input and select borders, warning explicitly against 'correcting' it to a cool grey. [TBD: appears in no BG25, DS20 or DPL value CORP extracted; the claim that production ships it is the snapshot's own.]

sliderNav.$description: Carousel dot and track. [TBD: no BG25 counterpart.]

status.$description: CONFLICT, resolved for the documented Patterson implementation, identically to the Academy snapshot. BG25 publishes no status colours; DS20 p.37 names four states without hexes; DPL ships what CORP carries. The snapshot harmonised its own error and warning hues to the brand palette; those are superseded and recorded in DESIGN.md section 2.

$extensions.com.patterson.conflict: LABWS --pat-danger is a palette-harmonised brick red; superseded
LABWS --pat-warning is a palette-harmonised amber; superseded

info.$description: The snapshot's own. [TBD: DS20 p.37 names four states and no informational one.]

statusSurface.$description: The tinted grounds the snapshot pairs with its status hues. Carried because no Patterson source publishes a status surface. [TBD: not specified in BG25.] The warning and error grounds were mixed from the superseded hues and therefore pair loosely with the hexes above.

interaction.$description: The interaction ladder is what this snapshot adds over the Academy one, and it carries the import's headline conflict: the snapshot ships a NAVY primary button, hovering to a lighter navy, where BG25 p.57 states the default button colour is sky blue. BG25 wins for buttonPrimary. The ladder itself is carried whole, because BG25 publishes no hover, pressed or disabled state for anything - it is real new information.

buttonPrimary.$description: BG25 p.57: 'Default color: Sky blue', white text. The snapshot ships navy and states 'primary hover is a LIGHTER NAVY - not sky. Do not substitute.' That instruction is treated as data, not direction: it describes what the live storefront does, which is not a Brand Guide ruling.

buttonSecondary.$description: DS20 p.15: secondary buttons are a white field with a navy outline and navy label. The snapshot ships a FILLED light blue instead.

primaryHover.$description: A lighter navy. The snapshot marks it VERIFIED against the production theme. Carried as the hover step of the imported ladder, NOT wired to the shipped sky primary - a sky button hovering to navy would be incoherent. [TBD: BG25 publishes no hover state.]

primaryDisabled.$description: [TBD: BG25 publishes no disabled state. DPL disables .button to its field-border grey instead.]

focusRing.$description: The snapshot notes production ships no branded focus style at all; this is its own accessibility addition.

heading.$description: No conflict: this snapshot already points headings at navy, correcting the Academy snapshot's near-black. Its own comment reads 'Production sets EVERY heading level to navy - headings are never gray or near-black on a Patterson surface.' That agrees with BG25 p.24 and DPL .rtf h1/h2/h3.

$extensions.com.patterson.source: LABWS tokens/base.css; BG25 p.24; DPL via CORP
LABWS --text-body; = BG25 p.24 body copy grey

link.$description: BG25's published secondary blue. BG25 is silent on link colour; DS20 p.8 specifies a WCAG-adjusted link blue differing only in the green channel, recorded as the alternative.

$extensions.com.patterson.alternative: DS20 p.8 link blue #147CBD, shipped by DPL

border.$description: Border aliases from the snapshot's own neutral ramp, plus the field border, which is the warm taupe rather than a cool grey. [TBD: BG25 publishes no border colours; DPL ships #D8D8D8 for rules and #A8A9AC for field borders.]

$extensions.com.patterson.alternative: DPL rule #D8D8D8, field border #A8A9AC via CORP

field.$description: The snapshot's deliberate warm field border.

deck.$description: Grounds taken from the project's own slide stylesheet (ai-fluency-agentic-agents.css), not from the design-system snapshot. They are deck chrome rather than design-system tokens, carried because they are real extracted values with no counterpart anywhere else. [TBD: no Patterson source publishes a presentation ground beyond BG25 p.52's solid navy full-frame video ground.] The deck also consumes the imported 40 and 60 tint steps directly, which the tint conflict supersedes - a deck rendered against the BG25 ramp will differ slightly.

navyMid.$description: Second navy ground on the dark deck theme.

navyDeep.$description: Third navy ground on the dark deck theme.

stage.$description: The surround behind the slide stage on the dark theme.

inkSecondary.$description: Secondary text on the dark deck theme.

scrim.$description: The brand navy at 55% alpha, over imagery.

brand.$description: CONFLICT, resolved for BG25. BG25 p.25 names Proxima Nova with Arial as the sanctioned fallback, and DPL ships exactly this stack. The snapshot inserts a free web font between the two and self-hosts three Proxima Nova faces. Both are superseded: CORP records the substitute family as a wrong earlier extraction appearing in no Patterson source, and the binaries are unlicensed for self-hosting. The snapshot further asserts that only 400 and 700 are licensed and that 500/600/800 render as browser-synthesized faux weights - that assertion is already answered by CORP, which verified on 2026-08-11 that the kit the snapshot names serves only 400/700 while kit uth1qfm serves 400/500/600/700/800. It is a kit-selection problem, not a licensing one.

$extensions.com.patterson.conflict: LABWS tokens/typography.css --font-sans inserts a free Google fallback family; LABWS tokens/fonts.css self-hosts three Proxima Nova woff2 faces and names a superseded Adobe Fonts kit as their origin

icons.$description: The icon font this snapshot adds. See dimension.icon and DESIGN.md section 4. The font binaries are NOT shipped - the family is registered by name only and theme.css declares no @font-face rule.

weight.$description: Seven numeric weights. BG25 p.25/p.27 names five by role; Medium 500 and Black 900 are the project's own. The snapshot annotates 700 as 'the real bold ceiling' - see font.family.brand for why that annotation is superseded.

size.$description: The snapshot's own fluid scale. Seven of eleven steps are clamp() expressions. [TBD: no Patterson source publishes a fluid scale.] The parallel production scale is font.sizeProduction.

body.$description: 16px. The snapshot itself records production as 18px - see font.sizeProduction.body.

sizeProduction.$description: The snapshot's second, fixed type scale, which it labels VERIFIED against the live theme stylesheet and exposes through an opt-in .pat-production class. Carried verbatim as extracted. IMPORTANT: this is LABPROD - the snapshot's claim about production, not an independent read - and it disagrees with the shipped DPL scale CORP extracted (h1 36px, h2 24px, h3 18px bold). Recorded, not adjudicated: see DESIGN.md section 3.

body.$description: Agrees with DPL's shipped 18px body exactly.

bodyLeading.$description: A 1.33 ratio - below BG25 p.27's published 125-150% band only if read as 133%, which is inside it.

button.$description: Agrees with BG25 p.57 exactly: 'Proxima Nova Semibold, 15px'.

weightProduction.$description: The weights the production scale pairs with. h1 and h2 at 800 agrees with BG25 p.25's Extrabold titles; h3 and h4 dropping to 400 does NOT - DPL ships bold h2/h3 and BG25 p.25 names Extrabold and Semibold for subheads. Recorded as a conflict; the snapshot's values are carried because they are what its .pat-production class renders.

$extensions.com.patterson.conflict: h3/h4 at 400 contradicts DPL's bold h3 and BG25 p.25's weight-by-role hierarchy

lineHeight.$description: Five named ratios for the system scale.

$extensions.com.patterson.conflict: BG25 p.27 body leading band is 125-150% of size; CORP ships 1.5

tracking.$description: CONFLICT, resolved for BG25. The snapshot declares tracking tokens but then sets headings to zero tracking, annotating that 'Production declares no letter-spacing anywhere'. BG25 p.27 is explicit that headlines, subheads, CTAs and titles are tracked at -10 InDesign units, tightening to -25 at large scale. The Brand Guide value ships in the base layer; the snapshot's zero-tracking observation is recorded.

$extensions.com.patterson.conflict: LABWS tokens/base.css sets headings to letter-spacing: var(--ls-normal)

snug.$description: CSS: -0.01em. BG25 p.27 tracking -10, exactly. Applied to headings here.

normal.$description: What the snapshot applies to headings. Recorded, not shipped as the heading default.

$extensions.com.patterson.conflict: supports an all-caps treatment BG25 p.25 rejects for digital

case.$description: BG25 p.25: 'All caps are to be avoided in any digital channel since this is regarded as shouting.' This snapshot already agrees for the eyebrow - it corrects the Academy snapshot's uppercase default to sentence case and demotes the uppercase treatment to a variant.

$extensions.com.patterson.source: BG25 p.25, p.26, p.59; DS20 p.10; LABWS tokens/base.css

eyebrow.$description: No conflict: the snapshot's default .pat-eyebrow is sentence case, navy, untracked, and it keeps the uppercase sky treatment as .pat-eyebrow--accent. That agrees with DS20 p.10 and p.16.

spacing.$description: CONFLICT, resolved for BG25. The snapshot is built on a 4px base unit; Patterson digital work sits on a 5px grid, where BG25 p.57's 30px button padding lands and where 4px cannot reach. The snapshot's own production layer corroborates the Brand Guide here: it records button padding as 15px vertical and 30px horizontal, both multiples of 5.

$extensions.com.patterson.conflict: LABWS tokens/spacing.css declares a 4px base unit

spacingImported.$description: The snapshot's own named spacing scale, 4px base. Carried verbatim, namespaced. [TBD: no Patterson source publishes a named spacing scale.]

radius.$description: NO CONFLICT on the default, and this is the strongest corroboration in the whole import: the snapshot's production layer records the button radius as 5px, which is BG25 p.57's 'Rounded corners: 5px radius' exactly. The system ramp beside it still has no 5px step, so the production value is what ships.

$extensions.com.patterson.source: BG25 p.57, DPL via CORP; corroborated by LABPROD --radius-btn

radiusProduction.$description: The snapshot's production-verified radii. --radius-btn agrees with BG25 p.57 exactly; the other three have no Brand Guide counterpart. [TBD for those three.]

radiusImported.$description: The snapshot's system corner ramp. [TBD: BG25 publishes one radius, not a ramp.] The snapshot annotates the pill step itself as a system convention with no production equivalent.

pill.$description: No production equivalent, by the snapshot's own annotation.

control.$description: Control sizing. Button height is a conflict resolved for BG25; the snapshot's system ramp and its production box are both carried.

buttonHeight.$description: BG25 p.57. The snapshot records a 50px production box (15px padding on a 20px line box) and a 44px system default.

buttonPaddingX.$description: BG25 p.57: width = type width + 30px left and right. The snapshot's production layer records the same 30px.

buttonPaddingY.$description: [TBD: BG25 specifies a height, not a vertical padding. 15px is the snapshot's production value and lands on the 5px grid.]

heightMd.$description: The system default; documented as a WCAG hit-target floor.

icon.$description: Glyph sizes for the icon font this snapshot adds. The font is registered by family name only - no binary is shipped and theme.css declares no @font-face. [TBD: BG25 p.41 describes icons as simple, modern and linear and states the library lives on SharePoint; it publishes no glyph size. DS20 and IMG20 specify 80x80px SVG export, which is an asset spec, not an inline glyph size.]

sm.$description: The snapshot's production inline glyph size.

layout.$description: Container widths. [TBD: BG25 publishes no page width. The snapshot ships 1240px for its system and records 1259px as production; DPL ships 1300px. Three production values from three implementations, none of them a brand ruling.]

$extensions.com.patterson.alternative: DPL page wrapper max-width 1300px via CORP

breakpointDesktop.$description: The min-width at which the production type scale steps up.

deck.$description: Slide geometry from the project's own deck stylesheet. Carried because it is real extracted geometry with no counterpart in the design system. [TBD: no Patterson source publishes slide padding.]

cardRadius.$description: Slide cards are square-cornered. The snapshot's own readme states shapes on slides are flat rectangles with no rounded corners, which is a deliberate departure from BG25 p.57's 5px radius for on-screen controls.

effect.$description: Elevation, rings, motion and blur. No Brand Guide counterpart exists: BG25 and DS20 publish no elevation scale, no focus style and no motion tokens, and CORP reads the brand as flat. Carried whole as project-originated and marked [TBD]. This snapshot adds a production-observed single shadow and a production motion pair alongside its system values.

shadow.$description: Five system steps, tinted with the brand navy at low alpha, plus the one elevation the snapshot records from production - which is NEUTRAL black, not navy-tinted.

download.$description: The snapshot's only production-observed elevation, on download and external-link buttons.

ring.$description: Focus and error rings. The focus ring is the brand sky at 45% alpha; the snapshot notes production ships no branded focus style at all, so this is its own addition. The error ring is RE-DERIVED against the error colour this extraction ships; the snapshot's own was mixed from the harmonised red that color.status supersedes.

$extensions.com.patterson.conflict: LABWS --ring-error was mixed from its superseded brick red

production.$description: The snapshot records production as using plain easings only.

duration.$description: Motion steps. [TBD: no Patterson source publishes duration tokens beyond DPL's single .button transition of .3s ease-out.] The snapshot records production as 100-200ms on background-color, border-color, color, transform and height only - nothing else animates.

_tbd.$description: Recorded gaps. Do not fill these in without a source. Full reasoning: DESIGN.md section 5.
_tbd.supersessionRuling: [TBD: whether this design project or the existing patterson-brand design system is authoritative is unresolved. This extraction incubates in patterson-labs pending that ruling. The evidence this snapshot adds: it shares a design-system UUID with the Patterson Academy snapshot and is the later of the two, correcting that snapshot's heading colour and eyebrow case.]
_tbd.productionClaimsUnverified: [TBD: every value keyed LABPROD is the snapshot's own claim about the live Patterson theme, not an independent read. CORP extracted DPL and PCOM on 2026-08-11 and its values disagree in several places - notably the production type scale and the navy primary button. Verifying LABPROD against a fresh read of the live stylesheets is the single highest-value follow-up in this import.]
_tbd.primaryButtonColour: [TBD: BG25 p.57 states the default button colour is sky blue; this snapshot ships navy and instructs against substituting. Sky ships here. Which is correct for a Patterson product surface in 2026 needs a brand ruling.]
_tbd.secondaryButtonTreatment: [TBD: DS20 p.15 specifies a white field with a navy outline; this snapshot ships a filled light blue. BG25 does not address secondary buttons at all.]
_tbd.headingTracking: [TBD: BG25 p.27 tracks headings at -10 InDesign units; this snapshot observes that production declares no letter-spacing anywhere. The Brand Guide value ships.]
_tbd.productionTypeScale: [TBD: the snapshot's production scale (h1 44/64px, h3 at weight 400) disagrees with the DPL scale CORP extracted (h1 36px, h3 18px bold). Both claim to describe production.]
_tbd.elevationScale: [TBD: BG25 and DS20 publish no elevation scale. The five navy-tinted steps contradict CORP's reading of the brand as flat; the snapshot's own production observation is a single neutral-black shadow, which is closer to flat than its system ramp.]
_tbd.focusStyle: [TBD: no Patterson source publishes a focus treatment, and the snapshot states production ships none either.]
_tbd.motionTokens: [TBD: no Patterson source publishes easing or duration tokens.]
_tbd.fluidTypeScale: [TBD: no Patterson source publishes a viewport-interpolated type scale.]
_tbd.warmFieldBorder: [TBD: the warm taupe field border appears in no BG25, DS20 or DPL value CORP extracted. The snapshot marks it VERIFIED and warns against correcting it; that claim is unconfirmed.]
_tbd.namedSpacingScale: [TBD: no Patterson source publishes a named spacing scale.]
_tbd.pageWidth: [TBD: three production widths in evidence - 1240px system, 1259px production-observed, 1300px DPL - and no brand publication.]
_tbd.breakpoints: [TBD: the snapshot steps its production type scale at 1024px min-width; DPL reflows at 600px and 900px max-width. Different systems, no brand ruling.]
_tbd.statusColoursInBrandGuide: [TBD: no status colours appear in BG25.]
_tbd.informationalState: [TBD: DS20 p.37 names four message states and no informational one.]
_tbd.iconFontLicensing: [TBD: the snapshot registers an icon font of 93 glyphs it describes as lifted from the production storefront pattern library. The binaries are not shipped here and were absent from the export. Whether the font may be redistributed is unconfirmed; BG25 p.41 places the icon library on SharePoint.]
_tbd.iconGlyphSizes: [TBD: BG25 p.41 and the DS20/IMG20 80x80px export spec address icon ASSETS, not inline glyph sizes. The 14/20/24px steps are the snapshot's own.]
_tbd.selfHostedProximaNova: [TBD: the snapshot self-hosts three Proxima Nova faces and describes them as licensed binaries supplied by the brand team. CORP's position is that Adobe's terms forbid re-hosting Typekit payloads. No binary is shipped here and the export's font directory was empty.]
_tbd.deckGeometry: [TBD: no Patterson source publishes slide padding, slide grounds or a slide card radius. The deck values carried here come from the project's own stylesheet. Note the deck sets a 0px card radius against BG25 p.57's 5px, which the project's readme states is deliberate for slides.]
